title: Weighted Sequence-Length Bucketing and Kernel-Fit Scheduler to Minimize Padding
author: Sofia Patel
description:
Motivation: current batching heuristics group by coarse sequence-length buckets which reduces padding for common workloads but struggles when model-kernel performance varies across length ranges and quantization profiles. This PR introduces a weighted bucketing strategy plus a kernel-fit scheduler that jointly optimizes padding cost and kernel throughput fit, and integrates an async flush policy that reduces tail-latency for sparse long-sequence traffic.

Design summary: the change has three primary pieces: 1) Weighted Sequence-Length Buckets: instead of fixed-width buckets we compute a dynamic bucket boundary set per model based on recent sequence-length distribution and a padding-cost function. Buckets are scored by expected bytes-of-padding * weight(seqlen) where weight accounts for kernel throughput and quantization penalty. 2) Kernel-Fit Scheduler: a lightweight scoring function picks which bucket to flush based on combined score = latency_penalty * alpha + (padding_cost) * beta + kernel_fit_bonus. Kernel_fit_bonus prefers dispatching batches to kernels measured to have better throughput at that sequence-length range (collected from runtime telemetry). 3) Async flush + KV-cache warmup hints: for buckets with heterogeneous seqlen we perform bounded async flushes when estimated wait time exceeds a threshold; concurrently we issue KV-cache warmup probes for the dominant sequence prefix in the bucket so that subsequent decoding steps avoid cold-KV penalties.

Implementation notes: changes live in runtime/batcher/ and runtime/scheduler/ with a small config surface exposed via model-profiles. The scoring and bucket recomputation run in a sampling background task (low CPU). We store per-model bucket metadata in the runtime metadata store; schema is backward compatible. New knobs added: model.profile.bucket_target_cost, scheduler.alpha, scheduler.beta, scheduler.kernel_fit_threshold, bucket.async_flush_ms.

Behavioral checklist (also in PR description):
- [x] Generate bucket boundaries from empirical seqlen histogram (sliding window 30m)
- [x] Compute per-bucket expected padding cost using token-cost and latency SLO weight
- [x] Integrate kernel-fit bonus using runtime kernel benchmarks
- [x] Add async flush path with bounded concurrency to avoid queue amplification
- [x] Emit metrics: redwood.batcher.bucket_size, redwood.batcher.padding_bytes_est, redwood.scheduler.kernel_fit_score
- [x] Add unit tests for bucket reclustering and scheduler scoring
- [x] Add e2e perf test and compare against current production bucketing

Testing & results: microbenchmarks were run on a dedicated perf-cluster (p4d-like) with synthetic traffic mimicking a 70/25/5 short/medium/long split. Baselines: main (fixed-width buckets) and previous histogram-bucketed approach. Results: overall token-cost reduced 11.7% (95% CI ±1.2%), mean latency improved 6.4%, p95 latency improved 9.8% under steady load. For mixed-quantization setups (int8/4bit combos) padding-driven kernel mismatch p95 dropped by 14%. KV-cache hit rate for decoding prefix warmups rose by 3.2 percentage points for long-tail workloads.

Compatibility and rollout: feature gated by model.profile.bucketing=v2. Default remains legacy bucketer until rollout. We added a canary rollout config that enables the scheduler for 5% of traffic per model. No protocol changes to API. Backwards compatible model profile parsing.

Files changed (high-level): runtime/batcher/bucketer.py (new), runtime/batcher/bucketer_test.py (new), runtime/scheduler/kernel_fit.py (new), runtime/scheduler/async_flush.py (mod), runtime/telemetry/bucket_metrics.go (mod), infra/perf/harness/bucket_perf.py (new), configs/model_profiles/schema_v2.yaml (mod), docs/observability/buckets.md (new).

Commits summary:
- feat(batcher): initial weighted-seqlen-bucketer with histogram reclustering
- feat(scheduler): kernel-fit scoring and dispatch API
- perf(test): add e2e perf harness and comparison script
- fix(async): bound concurrent async flushes to prevent amplification
- docs: observability and rollout notes for bucket v2

Review conversation highlights:
- Ethan Moore (review): "Nice design; two asks: (1) ensure bucket recompute cost is bounded under high traffic and (2) add a regression threshold in e2e so we don't rollout if p95 increases."
- Author reply: "Added sliding-window sampling and bounded recompute; added regression gate to perf harness (see infra/perf/harness/bucket_perf.py)."
- Priya Nair (review): "Kernel-fit bonus makes sense but we should avoid overfitting to noisy kernel microbenchmarks."
- Author reply: "Kernel-fit uses exponentially-weighted moving average with minimum sample counts; fallback to neutral bonus if noisy."
- Liam Chen (approval): "Approach is pragmatic and observability is solid. Approve once CI passes and we have canary config."

CI: unit, integration, lint, and perf smoke runs passed. One flaky test (telemetry export) was retried and passed.

Release notes: "Introduce weighted sequence-length bucketing and a kernel-fit scheduler that reduces padding and improves kernel utilization for mixed-length workloads. Feature is behind model profile flag."
